question: In hockey, what is the meaning of the signal if the umpire points both arms horizontally towards the goal?
solution:
The correct answer is Penalty corner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If the **umpire raises both arms horizontally in the direction of the goal,** it is a **penalty corner **of the signal.
 
• A **defensive violation** within the **penalty circle** or a willful violation within the **defensive 23-meter zone** results in a **penalty corner** being issued.
 
• A **penalty corner**, sometimes referred to as a short corner in field **hockey**, is a sanction imposed on the opposing side.
 
• **Attacking players** seek them out eagerly because they offer a great chance to score. **Players** learn specialised abilities for this phase of the game, such as the** drag flick,** and there are specific rules that only apply in **penalty corners.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hockey **

 
 
• ​The term "**hockey**" refers to a **group of different summer and winter team games** that were first played on an **outdoor field,** **a sheet of ice, or a dry floor,** like in a **gymnasium**. While the specific regulations, player counts, attire, and most notably the playing field differ amongst these games, they all include two opposing teams utilising sticks to direct a ball or disc towards a goal.
 
• **Hockey comes in a variety of forms**.
 
• Skates, whether wheeled or bladed, are used in some games yet not in others.
 
• The word "**hockey**" is frequently followed by another word, such as "f**ield hockey," "ice hockey," "roller hockey," "rink hockey," or "floor hockey,"** to assist distinguish between these different games.
